title: Bridging AI-Assisted Cancer Screening and Public Health Surveillance: Evidence and Challenges in the Philippines (2020–2026)
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping cancer screening globally, yet evidence supporting its clinical application and integration into public health systems remains limited in countries such as the Philippines. This narrative review synthesised documented Philippine applications of AI-assisted cancer screening from January 2020 to September 2026, examining their implications for cancer surveillance, health-system readiness, and policy. A structured review of scientific publications, government and health technology assessment documents, and grey literature revealed a limited and heterogeneous evidence base. Only two peer-reviewed studies reported separately identifiable Philippine patient data, both retrospective, addressing mammography classification and computer-aided colonoscopy. Multinational evaluations and reported commercial deployments suggested opportunities for AI-assisted detection but provided insufficient Philippine-specific evidence of clinical effectiveness and patient outcomes. No prospective validation studies in Filipino screening populations or local evaluations of AI-assisted cervical or liver cancer screening were identified. Beyond clinical validation, major barriers included predominantly opportunistic screening, incomplete population-based cancer registry implementation, fragmented digital infrastructure, workforce constraints, regulatory uncertainty, and insufficient economic evaluation. Recent national screening financing policies provide opportunities for integrating innovative technologies into established healthcare pathways. These findings underscore that the transition toward AI-assisted cancer screening requires not only technological advancement but also locally validated evidence, strengthened population-based surveillance, equitable access, and coordinated public health governance.
